name: High Fjell Border
inspired_by: The European High North as of 2026: a Finnmark-type fjord coast and fell plateau in northern Norway, a Lapland-type birch and pine border valley with Finland, and the land border with Russia's Kola peninsula on the east edge, where the Northern Fleet is based. Allied winter exercises, GPS jamming, cable and infrastructure incidents and Arctic shipping define the grey zone. All towns are fictional.
climate: Subarctic (Koppen Dfc) inland, subpolar oceanic (Cfc) on the coast warmed by the Atlantic current. Winters -10 to -30 C inland, -3 to -10 C on the coast; summers 10-18 C. Polar night for about 2 months, midnight sun for about 2.5 months. 350-700 mm precipitation, much as snow; snow cover October/November-May.
seasons: Polar night (late Nov-mid Jan): no sunrise, blue twilight at midday, aurora, deep cold
Late winter (Feb-Apr): returning light, best snow for skis and snowmobiles, frozen lakes and rivers, blizzards
Spring thaw (May-Jun): slush, flooding rivers, ice break-up, impassable terrain
Midnight sun (Jun-Aug): 24 h daylight, mosquitoes, reindeer on the coast
Autumn (Sep-Oct): ruska colours, first snow, storms on the coast

vegetation: bare rock and lichen on headlands
dwarf birch (Betula nana) and willow scrub
bogs (aapa mires) with sedge and cloudberry
none (water): deep fjords, drift ice in sheltered heads in winter

terrain.relief: Steep fjords cut into a rolling fell plateau at 300-600 m with rounded summits to 1,100 m in the west; the plateau falls south-east into a wide forested river valley (50-150 m) that forms the border on the east edge; countless lakes and boulder fields.
features: a border river with a hydro dam and a single crossing
terrain.water: Fjords and the sea on the north and west edges; a border river with a hydro dam; hundreds of lakes; everything frozen from November to May except the sea and fast water.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m with bathymetry. Plateau from fbm; fjords carved as deep U-shaped troughs along ridged-noise valleys reaching the coast; glacial lakes as many cellular depressions; border river valley as a wide spline basin. Snow cover is a season-dependent material layer over everything (depth 0.3-1.5 m) that changes mobility.
generator.erosion: Glacial look rather than fluvial: smooth with a low-pass filter on the plateau, steepen fjord walls; light hydraulic pass for streams.
generator.rivers: Border river spline along the east edge with rapids and a dam; streams by flow accumulation into lakes; lake levels by basin fill.
generator.settlement_flattening: Fishing villages on fjord-side terraces; border-valley villages along the river road.
generator.notes: Cold and darkness are the main hazards: snowmobiles, skis and tracked vehicles (BV206/BvS10-type) are the mobility layer; AAVs useless off the coast; helicopters grounded in blizzards. Proposed cold-exposure mechanic ties to the medical model.

settlements.architecture: Fishing villages on the fjords: one- and two-storey timber houses painted red, white and yellow with steep metal roofs, fish-drying racks, a harbour with quays, a fish processing plant, a church, a school and a shop; houses on concrete foundations with storm porches.
settlements.wall_class: Timber thin; concrete foundations and plant walls medium.
layout_rules: harbour and fish plant as the centre

settlements.architecture: Border-region town: timber and concrete houses, a 1950s-rebuilt centre of two- to four-storey concrete blocks, a garrison, a hotel, a port with an ice-free quay, a mining or hydro industry site.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete blocks thick; timber houses thin.
layout_rules: port and industrial strip on the fjord

settlements.architecture: Sami reindeer-herding sites and hut camps: timber cabins, lavvu tents, corrals and fences; seasonal.

Military and infrastructure: a border garrison with barracks and vehicle sheds, a coastal radar station with domes, a hydro dam and powerhouse, a satellite ground station of white domes, a deep-water port, an army winter-training camp of tents and huts, border posts with towers.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete thick; sheds and tents thin.
layout_rules: radar and satellite domes on summits and headlands
winter camp in the birch forest

infrastructure.roads: One coastal road with tunnels and a ferry, one road along the border river to the crossing, few others; winter snowmobile trails.
infrastructure.rail: Iron-ore railway to a port at the south-west edge (electrified single track, snow sheds).
infrastructure.power: Hydro dam on the border river, power lines across the fells, wind farm on a plateau.
infrastructure.ports: Deep-water ice-free port, fishing harbours, a coastguard base; LHD in a fjord.
infrastructure.airfields: Small regional airport on a plateau (AI aircraft); helipads.
infrastructure.checkpoints: One border crossing (closed to most traffic) with a fence and posts; police checks on the coastal road during exercises.

pois.description: Field of white antenna domes on a summit plateau with a control building, a fence and a road; cable to the coast.
pois.contract_use: Arctic infrastructure security; counter-sabotage guard (clients nor, usa)

pois.description: Radar station on a headland with domes, a mast, a bunker and a winding road; GPS-jamming monitoring.
pois.contract_use: site security; recover a sensor buoy that washed ashore

pois.description: The single crossing with gates, a customs hall, a fence and towers; a garrison nearby; Russian posts visible across the river.
pois.contract_use: border security patrol; drone incursion response (clients nor, fin)

pois.description: Dam on the border river with a powerhouse, a spillway and a road across; Russia-side bank in view.
Crash site on the fell plateau of a light aircraft or helicopter in snow; survivors in a snow shelter.
pois.contract_use: Arctic search and recovery (clients can, nor, usa)

pois.description: Exercise equipment lost in a blizzard (sensor kit, a tracked vehicle through lake ice) on a frozen lake.
pois.contract_use: recover lost equipment or sensitive kit (clients usa, gbr, nor)

pois.description: Fishing harbour with a fish plant, quays, trawlers and drying racks.
pois.contract_use: port security; boarding of a suspicious trawler

pois.description: Foreign-flagged trawler loitering over a seabed cable route; crew refuses inspection.
pois.contract_use: boarding support for the coastguard (clients nor, dnk)

pois.description: Allied winter-training camp: tents, huts, snowmobile park, tracked carriers, a range.
Iron-ore loading port with conveyor gantries, ship loader, rail yard and storage halls.
pois.contract_use: counter-sabotage guard on the rail line

pois.description: Remote cabin on a border lake, used by a sabotage team as a hide; snowmobile tracks lead to the border.
Small polar research station with labs, a weather mast and accommodation; international scientists.
pois.contract_use: evacuation in a storm; protect researchers

weather.visibility_notes: Whiteout drops visibility to metres and grounds aircraft; polar night needs NVGs or white light; snow glare in spring; aurora gives faint light.
weather.dust_or_snow: Snow cover October/November-May; drifting snow in wind.

civilians.behaviour: Small, spread-out population; fishermen, miners, reindeer herders with herds on the plateau, tourists in summer. People shelter indoors in storms; herders move with reindeer on seasonal routes and may be on the plateau in any weather.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Low density; reindeer herders on the plateau are the main risk in open-terrain fights.

factions_present.where: Coast, border garrison and crossing, radar and satellite stations, ports.
South-east border valley and forest (the Finnish side of the composite map).
Contingent at the winter-training camp; ore railway security at the south-west edge.
Marines with prepositioned equipment at the winter camp; maritime patrol aircraft (AI).
Commando winter-training detachment at the camp.
Arctic training detachment and search-and-rescue liaison.
Naval patrol vessel and Arctic command liaison.
Researchers at the polar research station and an observer team (plausibility: Japan's Arctic role is research and diplomacy).
Beyond the east-edge border: posts, the Kola-side garrison; GPS jamming, drones, sabotage teams, trawlers over cables.

frontline: Grey zone. The border does not move; rus events (GPS jamming, drone overflights of infrastructure, sabotage teams, cable incidents, airspace probes) raise alert levels and post infrastructure-security, recovery and boarding contracts. Weather drives availability: blizzards pause operations and post search-and-rescue contracts. A late-game escalation scenario (proposed) sees rus cross the border river, with the fell plateau as the battle space.
contract_hooks: Arctic search and recovery of a crashed aircraft crew in a blizzard (clients can, nor)
Satellite ground station security against sabotage (clients nor, usa)
Recover lost equipment from lake ice after an exercise (clients usa, gbr, nor)
Boarding support on a trawler loitering over a cable route (clients nor, dnk)
Counter-sabotage raid on a border lake cabin (clients nor, fin)
Border security patrol during a drone incursion (clients nor, fin)
Evacuate researchers from the polar station ahead of a storm (clients jpn, nor)
Escalation scenario: delay an advance across the fell plateau (late game)

hot_zones.name: Fell plateau escalation (late game, fictional what-if)
hot_zones.layout: rus HQ across the border; 4 outposts on summits and at lake narrows; checkpoints at the crossing and dam; roaming ski and snowmobile patrols; 1-2 QRF tracked-vehicle groups

insertion.fob: LHD in a fjord for coastal contracts (ice-free); inland FOB at the allied winter-training camp. Mobility by tracked carriers, snowmobiles and skis; helicopters weather-limited; AAVs only in fjords.
